source.title: Hadronic Decay Branching Ratio Measurements of the Higgs Boson at Future Colliders Using the Holistic Approach
source.authors: Yong-Feng Zhu; Jianfeng Jiang; Chao Yang; Man-Qi Ruan

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study examines training-data scaling in a supervised particle-physics classifier, a different application from language-model pretraining, and reports scaling results in that setting.
record.gate_note: The paper cites LLM scaling laws as an analogy, then measures its own classifier's performance as training-data size changes. It does not test language-model held-out cross-entropy, parameter-count or compute scaling, or a compute-optimal allocation. The numerical Higgs measurement precisions that are not about scaling are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. Its measures are classifier accuracy, per-class efficiencies and a derived physics statistical uncertainty (sqrt(S+B)/S), not held-out loss. The power law y = aN^-α + c is used as an ansatz to describe and extrapolate its own learning curves (Sec. 4.2, 4.4). It reports no exponent, coefficients or goodness of fit, so the results cannot show whether the power-law form holds. LLM scaling laws are cited only as an analogy. The data-scaling observations are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Additions: the authors present the scaling behaviour mainly as a diagnostic, used to monitor the model, optimise analysis tactics and quantify uncertainties. They say gains for cc̄, gg and ZZ* are not yet saturated. They say the analysis without pre-selection needs far more data and might surpass the pre-selected one only with abundant data.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales a supervised ParticleNet classifier with training-event count and examines classification and projected physics-measurement outcomes. It does not measure language-model pretraining loss or vary model size, tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by decay topology, hadronization generator (Pythia8 versus Herwig7), and whether pre-selection is applied.

fits_no_version.finding: In a supervised ParticleNet collider-event classifier, accuracy rises with training-set size along an S-curve: near-random below ~100 events, rapid gain to ~10^5, slow approach to ~86% at 10^6. Per-class efficiencies improve at topology-dependent rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In supervised scientific classifiers, accuracy versus training-data size follows a three-phase S-curve rather than a single power law.

fits_no_version.finding: A derived measurement uncertainty is described with a power law plus an irreducible floor in training-data size. For bb̄ it approaches the statistical limit; for ZZ* a gap remains. No exponents or fit quality are given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data-scaling of downstream physics-measurement precision saturates at a task-dependent floor.

fits_no_version.finding: With more training data, out-of-generator (Herwig7) performance converges for two-body decays but diverges for four-body decays. Pre-selection helps at small data, and the advantage shrinks with more data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gains from scaling training data can fail to transfer under simulator shift for complex topologies.

record.problems: The reported application is a simulated collider-event classifier rather than a language model. The text gives no fit coefficients or fit uncertainty for the scaling ansatz; several scaling results are described qualitatively from figures. The with-pre-selection curve beyond 10^5 events is extrapolated, and the paper notes unmodeled systematic and theoretical uncertainties.
record.rows_left_out: No additional scaling-related outcomes were left out. The paper's standalone Higgs branching-ratio precision projections and comparisons with other collider studies are not results about scaling with training-data size.

untested.parts: No language models or held-out pretraining loss; no parameter, token or compute scaling.
No small-to-large loss extrapolation is checked against measured large runs. The extrapolation in Sec. 4.4 is not validated.
No loss is measured and no power-law fit quality or exponent is reported; only training-set size is varied, model size is not.
No exponents are fitted or compared across fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The study is a Higgs-physics paper. Its LLM scaling laws (refs 26, 27) appear only as an analogy. Only training-set size is varied, never model size or compute. Internal inconsistency: Appendix A swaps the ZZ* values (6.31% vs 5.21%) relative to Table 2. Sec. 4.4 cites a nonexistent Eq. 4.2. The record's 'tests/T3' and its V5 labels are not justified: the power-law fit is an ansatz with no reported parameters or fit quality, on a non-loss measure.

versions.untested_parts: No language models, held-out pretraining cross-entropy, or scaling in parameters, tokens, or compute are tested.
No small-run language-model loss fits are evaluated against larger language-model runs.
No fixed-compute allocation between model parameters and training tokens is evaluated.
The study does not compare depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
The study tests training-data scaling in a supervised collider-event classifier, not held-out language-model loss. It does not test image/video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
No language-model downstream tasks or relationship between language-model pretraining loss and downstream performance is tested.

No language-model exponents or compute-optimal allocation are fitted or compared across fitting choices. The study does report scaling changes across generator and pre-selection settings, but in a different application.

rows.subject: ParticleNet (PN)
rows.operation_detail: Varied training dataset size and measured overall classification accuracy.
rows.baseline: Near-random classification in the trivial phase
rows.value: The text describes an S-curve: near-random until roughly 100 events, rapid improvement until roughly 10^5 events, then slower improvement; accuracy reaches approximately 86% at 10^6 events.
rows.note: This is classifier accuracy, not language-model loss; the text describes an S-curve rather than a single power law.
rows.check: The measure is overall classification accuracy, not loss, so it cannot bear on V5's power-law form. The text describes an S-curve (near-random to ~100 events, rapid gain to ~10^5, ~86% at 10^6). No fit is reported.
